summary: Thinlay Ram Shashni is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies as editor (attested 1997, 2007) and later as Associate Professor and In-charge/HoD (attested 2026).

Thinley Dorji Bhutia worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a Tibetan teacher and boarding superintendent at Darjeeling Government High School, and served as Director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and Chief Editor of Bulletin of Tibetology (attested 1994).

Thinley Norbu Rinpoche (1931–2011) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling Monastery under Dudjom Rinpoche (Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje) and founded the White Lotus School.

Thomas A. Forsthoefel specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Georgetown University, Loyola University Chicago, and the University of Chicago Divinity School under Paul J. Griffiths, later becoming associate professor of religious studies at Mercyhurst University (attested 2007).

Thomas A. Tweed (born 1954) is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his PhD from Stanford University under William R. Hutchison and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1993–2008).

Thomas Alexander Wise (1801–1889) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Indian Medical Service (1827–1851) and founded Hooghly Mohsin College in 1834, serving as its Principal.
Thomas Andrew Lumisden Strange (1756–1841) was an Indologist. He was educated at Westminster School and the University of Oxford, where he earned a B.A. and a D.C.L.

Thomas Athol Joyce (1878–1942) worked in history and archaeology. He studied at Dulwich College and Hertford College, Oxford (M.A.), and served as Deputy Keeper at the British Museum from 1902 to 1938.

Thomas B. Coburn (1944–2023) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Princeton and Harvard. He held academic posts at St. Lawrence University (~1974–2002) and Harvard University (~2008–2013).

Thomas B. Ellis specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Assistant Professor of Religion at Appalachian State University (attested 2009).

Thomas Best Jervis (1796–1857) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held appointments with the East India Company (~1813–1841), the Survey of India (~1819–1841), and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Thomas Blom Hansen (born 1958) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He held posts at the universities of Edinburgh, Yale, Amsterdam, and Natal, and became Professor of Anthropology at Stanford University in 2010. He also studied at Aalborg University.

Thomas Bond Lindsay (1853–1909) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. Educated at Wesleyan University and Boston University (Ph.D.), he taught at Newton High School and served as Assistant Professor of Latin and Sanskrit at Boston University (1878–1909).

Thomas Borchert specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. A former PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005), he became Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Bruce Ridgeway (1949–2005) specialized in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington, where he also served as Director from approximately 1986 to 1994.

Thomas Burrow (1909–1986) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai University. He worked at the British Museum and SOAS before serving as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Oxford (1944–1976).

Thomas Callan Hodson (1871–1953) studied at The Queen's College, Oxford. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he served as Registrar at Queen Mary University, Principal of Thornsey Training College, and Reader of Ethnography at Cambridge (1926–1937).

Thomas Candy (1804–1877) was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Magdalen College School. He served as Superintendent (1837) and Principal (1851–1857) at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

Thomas Chalmers (1780–1847) was a scholar in religious studies. He studied at the University of St Andrews and the University of Edinburgh, later holding posts at St Andrews (~1823–1828) and Edinburgh (~1828–1843).

Thomas Christian Tychsen (1758–1834) was a scholar of linguistics and history. He studied at Kiel and Göttingen, where he studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne and later became Professor of Theology (1785) and Professor of Philosophy (1788).
